case_scope.source_excerpt:
Let $d\ge0$ and $k\ge0$ be integers, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and convex, let $A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k$ be linear, let $b\in\mathbb R^k$, and let $x_*\in U$ satisfy $Ax_*=b$. Put $T=\ker A$. Assume $f:U\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable and has second directional derivatives represented by a continuous matrix field: there is a continuous map $H:U\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ with symmetric values, and for every $x\in U$ and $h\in\mathbb R^d$,

$$\left.\frac{d^2}{dt^2}f(x+th)\right|_{t=0}=Q_x(h):=h^{\mathsf T}H(x)h.$$

Assume stationarity $Df(x_*)h=0$ for every $h\in T$. If $Q_{x_*}(h_0)<0$ for some $h_0\in T$, then $x_*$ is not a local minimum of $f$ on $\{x\in U:Ax=b\}$. If $Q_{x_*}(h)>0$ for every nonzero $h\in T$, then $x_*$ is a strict local minimum on that feasible slice. If $T=\{0\}$, the latter conclusion holds because $x_*$ is the only feasible point.
case_scope.case_interpretation: The admitted x_* excludes an empty feasible slice. With no nonzero tangent direction (T={0}), the only feasible point is x_*; the d=0 singleton case is explicitly discharged in step1.1 and the general T={0} case in step3.1.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement distinguishes strict negative and positive curvature and makes no conclusion at Q=0.

derivations.claim: Suppose $h_0\in T$ and $Q_{x_*}(h_0)<0$. Set $\phi(t)=f(x_*+th_0)$ for $t$ near $0$. Openness of $U$ permits this definition; stationarity gives $\phi'(0)=0$. The identity in the Statement gives $\phi''(t)=Q_{x_*+th_0}(h_0)$ wherever defined, and continuity of the entries of $H$ makes this negative for every sufficiently small $t\ge0$.
derivations.owner_interface_clarification: The new initial branch discharges d=0 via the published zero-vector Euclidean convention; all remaining negative-curvature argument is unchanged and assumes d>=1.

derivations.claim: Suppose $T\ne\{0\}$ and $Q_{x_*}(h)>0$ for each nonzero $h\in T$. The unit sphere $S_T=\{h\in T:\|h\|_2=1\}$ is nonempty, closed by [L2] and continuity of the norm, and bounded; [L3] makes it compact. The quadratic polynomial $h\mapsto h^{\mathsf T}H(x_*)h$ is continuous, so [L4] gives $\lambda=\min_{h\in S_T}Q_{x_*}(h)>0$.

Choose such a small $t>0$. Applying [L5] to $\phi'$ on $[0,t]$ gives $\phi'(t)-\phi'(0)=t\phi''(s)<0$ for some $s\in(0,t)$, hence $\phi'(t)<0$; the same argument applies to every positive endpoint up to $t$. Applying [L5] to $\phi$ on $[0,t]$ gives $\phi(t)-\phi(0)=t\phi'(r)<0$ for some $r\in(0,t)$. Since $h_0\in\ker A$, $x_*+th_0$ is feasible, so $x_*$ is not a local minimum.

By continuity of the finitely many entries of $H$, choose $\delta>0$ so that $\|x-x_*\|_2<\delta$ implies $|Q_x(h)-Q_{x_*}(h)|<\lambda/2$ for every unit vector $h$: expand the difference as a finite sum of entry differences times $h_i h_j$, each with $|h_i h_j|\le1$. If $y\ne x_*$ is feasible and $\|y-x_*\|_2<\delta$, put $v=y-x_*$. Then $v\in T$, and convexity of $U$ keeps $x_*+tv$ in $U$ for $0\le t\le1$. For $\phi(t)=f(x_*+tv)$, stationarity gives $\phi'(0)=0$, while homogeneity of the quadratic form gives $\phi''(t)=Q_{x_*+tv}(v)\ge(\lambda/2)\|v\|_2^2>0$.

For any $t\in(0,1]$, [L5] applied to $\phi'$ on $[0,t]$ yields $\phi'(t)-\phi'(0)=t\phi''(s)>0$ for some $s\in(0,t)$, so $\phi'(t)>0$. Applying [L5] to $\phi$ on $[0,1]$ gives $\phi(1)-\phi(0)=\phi'(r)>0$ for some $r\in(0,1)$. Thus every distinct feasible $y$ with $\|y-x_*\|_2<\delta$ has $f(y)>f(x_*)$. If $T=\{0\}$, $Ay=Ax_*$ implies $y-x_*\in T=\{0\}$, so $x_*$ is the only feasible point.

The identity in the Statement gives $\phi''(t)=Q_{x_*+th_0}(h_0)$ wherever defined, and continuity of the entries of $H$ makes this negative for every sufficiently small $t\ge0$. If $y\ne x_*$ is feasible and $\|y-x_*\|_2<\delta$, put $v=y-x_*$. Then $v\in T$, and convexity of $U$ keeps $x_*+tv$ in $U$ for $0\le t\le1$. For $\phi(t)=f(x_*+tv)$, stationarity gives $\phi'(0)=0$, while homogeneity of the quadratic form gives $\phi''(t)=Q_{x_*+tv}(v)\ge(\lambda/2)\|v\|_2^2>0$. [F1, L1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 For any $t\in(0,1]$, [L5] applied to $\phi'$ on $[0,t]$ yields $\phi'(t)-\phi'(0)=t\phi''(s)>0$ for some $s\in(0,t)$, so $\phi'(t)>0$. Applying [L5] to $\phi$ on $[0,1]$ gives $\phi(1)-\phi(0)=\phi'(r)>0$ for some $r\in(0,1)$. Thus every distinct feasible $y$ with $\|y-x_*\|_2<\delta$ has $f(y)>f(x_*)$.
